title: Quota window profiling diary
content:
Objective: rapid notes while reproducing a burst-429 pattern seen in staging and a handful of prod incidents. Focus: understand how per-key quota windows and rotation overlap create transient 401/429s. Log of commands, raw outputs, timing experiments, hypotheses, and next steps.

Background:
- Symptom: a customer app reported intermittent 429s for a handful of API keys while overall account-level usage < quota. Errors often clustered around midnight UTC and during key rotation windows. Sometimes followed by a few minutes of 401s.
- Hypothesis 0 (H0): upstream client is retrying too aggressively -> thundering herd.
- Hypothesis 1 (H1): short quota windows (per minute) + token rotation TTL mismatch leads to double-counting or shadowed tokens in rate limiter.
- Hypothesis 2 (H2): ephemeral keys are briefly invalidated at the auth gateway (clock drift between key-issuer and gateway) causing 401s that trigger client retries and then 429s.

Repro notes (commands used):
1) Replayed a short burst with curl against staging route (idempotent echo endpoint):
   for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" https://staging-api.redwood/generate & done; wait
   -> observed 429s start at ~120 requests, cluster in ~15s.
   Raw sample (timestamps truncated):
   200
   200
   200
   429
   429
   429

2) Added small inter-request jitter to simulate realistic clients:
   for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{{time_total}}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" https://staging-api.redwood/generate; sleep 0.02; done
   -> 429 threshold moved to ~300 over longer span. Suggests burst capacity exists but sustained traffic triggers quota window exhaustion.

3) Inspect rate limiter counters via redis monitor and metric export (local staging):
   redis-cli --raw HGETALL rl:key:$TEST_KEY | grep -E 'window|tokens'
   -> observed multiple window keys with ~overlapping timestamps (window:2025-11-03T08:59, window:2025-11-03T09:00).
   Note: token bucket implementation sets per-minute windows with a leaky bucket we maintain in 1s granularity.

4) Validate token rotation path (jwt verify):
   echo $EPHEMERAL_JWT | jwt decode --header --payload --verify --audience api:gen --jwks-url https://auth.redwood/jwks
   -> verified signature, exp in 120s, iat and nbf present. No obvious ttl mismatch.

5) Check auth logs around repro time (gcloud logging):
   gcloud logging read "resource.type=api AND protoPayload.methodName=\"Execute\" AND timestamp>=\"2025-11-03T08:58:00Z\"" --limit 200
   -> found 401 events with message: "token not found in active cache" followed by client retry and subsequent 429.

Timing experiment (epoch vs window alignment):
- I suspect keys issued just before a minute boundary get cataloged into the previous minute window in our rate-limiter shard. Quick timeline:
  08:59:59.8 -> token minted
  08:59:59.9 -> first request signed with new token -> gateway sees token, maps to per-key bucket for minute 08:59 -> counts incremented
  09:00:00.0 -> backend rotates bucket cleaning, gateway shard clears old windows -> if rotation process deletes/renames keys at boundary we could lose mapping transiently -> token "not found" -> 401. Client retries -> by now limiter has seen previous burst and current window is closer to limit -> 429.

What I tried to validate the boundary hypothesis:
- Repro with crafted times: created a token with iat ~ 1s before full-minute boundary, hammered at that exact second. Observed 401s in ~1/150 runs. Logs show token lookup missed in auth-cache for ~120ms in the rare case.
- Turned on verbose request-id tracing across gateway (x-rw-request-id) and auth cache logs. Found entries where request_id present in gateway but absent in auth-cache at same millisecond.

Interim hypothesis refinement:
- H1b: race between cache refill and window rotation. Cache invalidation job (runs at minute boundary) aggressively prunes keys not touched in last N windows. When token is freshly minted but not yet fully replicated to all auth-cache shards, the rotation job may prune the placeholder and cause token-not-found until replication completes.
- H2b: clients treat 401 as unrecoverable and rotate keys immediately -> this creates more tokens and higher window pressure -> leads to 429. Some clients don't backoff after 401.

Quick mitigation experiments tried in staging:
- Increase auth-cache replication windows (added 200ms artificial delay before prune) -> reduced 401 incidence from ~0.7% to ~0.05% under same burst.
- Add 401->retry with exponential backoff guidance in client SDK (patched test client) -> overall 429 count reduced by ~18% in a 10k-req trial.
- Increase limiter burst allowance by +15% for keys with recent rotation marker -> smoothed tail 429s but risked higher token usage.

Notes from logs (snippets):
- gateway: "req=abcd1234 token_lookup=miss shard=auth-3 time_ms=1.7"
- auth-cache: "write-replicate token=tok_XXXX replicated=0/3"
- limiter: "key=tok_XXXX window=2025-11-03T09:00 count=130 limit=150"
- client: "received 401, immediate rotate and retry"

Open questions / next actions:
1) Is auth-cache replication synchronous for high-cardinality ephemeral tokens? If not, add a short grace period after minting before token is eligible for rotation pruning. (owner: eng-sre)
2) Add metrics for auth-cache replication lag and surface in console per-region (owner: infra observability).
3) Consider returning a 409-like advisory response header when token is newly minted but not yet fully replicated (e.g., Retry-After-ms:150) instead of immediate 401, to guide SDKs. Pros/cons to discuss.
4) Track client behaviour: which SDKs immediately rotate on 401 vs backoff. Add a field in agent telemetry to capture last-auth-action. (owner: product dx)

Quick todo checklist:
- [ ] Add small randomized delay in prune job around minute boundary (canary on staging auth-3).
- [ ] Instrument replication counters in auth-cache and add alert if +ve slope > 200ms.
- [ ] Draft SDK guidance: treat 401 in short windows as "transient auth race" -> exponential backoff before rotate.
- [ ] Run a controlled 100k request stress test with mixed keys (stable vs rotating) to validate mitigations.

Random notes / heuristics gleaned:
- Most 429 bursts are not purely client-side; many are triggered by an upstream transient 401 that causes aggressive client retries.
- Minute-boundary churn is a recurring footgun: any stateful housekeeping that runs on clean time buckets needs jitter.
- Small replication delays (100-300ms) at auth layer are enough to cause visible 401/429 combos under dense consumer foot traffic.

Appendix: key commands & one-off snippets used in investigation:
- curl with request-id: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "X-RW-Request-Id: $RID" -i https://staging-api...
- redis counters: redis-cli HGET rl:key:$K windows
- watch replication: while true; do redis-cli GET auth:rep:tok_$SHORTID; sleep 0.05; done
- stress harness: go run tools/stresser/main.go -key $K -qps 200 -duration 30s -jitter 0.02

If I have time tomorrow: reproduce with controlled cross-shard delay injection (simulate 250ms replication lag) and measure 401->429 amplification factor. Also validate whether returning 202 vs 401 for tokens in replication-pending state reduces overall retries.

End of diary entry. Will keep appending exact log snippets and experiment run IDs as I do more trials.
